messages:
priya: Quick idea 1: introduce a 'canary compatibility shim' for migrations where a quantized/optimized variant runs in front of the pinned model for a short window. Purpose: reduce unit cost and validate compatibility before full migration.

marc: Nice. How does the shim decide to fall back?

priya: Two mechanisms: deterministic output-check for n-grams on a test suite + a probabilistic compatibility_score on sampled production traffic. If compatibility_score < 0.95 OR output-check fails on >=1% of cases, auto-fallback.

selena: We need clear SLA language for customers who pin. They will want guaranteed rollback and a defined pin gracepath. What's the proposed window?

eric: From Ops perspective, keep canary short and incremental. Proposal: 3-day shadow, then ramp 2% -> 10% -> 25% -> 100% over 21 days, with hold checks at each step.

priya: Draft thresholds:

```
canary_shim_config:
  shadow_days: 3
  ramp_days_total: 21
  ramp_schedule_pct: [2, 10, 25, 100]
  compatibility_score_threshold: 0.95
  ngram_mismatch_pct_threshold: 1.0
  latency_overhead_ms: 20  # allowed added p95 latency compared to baseline
  cost_savings_target_pct: 15
```

marc: Also surface task-level metrics: accuracy/regression per benchmark suite, hallucination checkpoints, and end-to-end latency. Each hold needs a pass on all three families.

selena: Legal: if a customer pins, we can offer an "accelerated-migration" SOW that guarantees a 60-day pin and a documented rollback escrow (snapshot of workload prompts, pins, and bench outputs). But we cannot promise indefinite pins.

legal-bot: adding clause: "pin_gracepath_days: 60" and "rollback_escrow_included: true" to SOW template.

priya: Good. Tech runbook items:
- Preflight: run commonbench + customer-critical prompt set.
- Shadow: 3 days, collect compatibility_score and mismatch stats.
- Ramp: only if shadow pass. At each step, check compatibility_score and latency overhead.
- Auto-fallback: immediate if mismatch >= 1% or compatibility_score dips > 0.05 from baseline.

eric: Who owns the temporary capacity? During 25% and 100% steps Dedicated pools might need bursting. Eng-runtime must be looped in with a 72hr lead.

marc: Also add a metric we call "behavioral-regression-index" (BRI) that aggregates quality regressions across suites (0..1 scale). Block migration if BRI > 0.03.

selena: For customer opt-ins during the canary run, we should require an explicit acceptance signoff recorded in the ticket and an option for a paid extended pin (extra 30 days) for high-risk customers.

priya: catalog-bot: please create a tracking ticket for "canary-compat-shim + migration SOW" and attach SOW template.

catalog-bot: created ticket MGMT-5502: "canary compatibility shim + migration SOW" 0. Assignees: @priya, @marc, @eric.

marc: Ops ask: add an alerting rule: "canary_shim_mismatch_rate" -> Pager if >1% sustained over 5 minutes during ramp. Also a Console dashboard panel for compat_score trend.

eric: We'll add a step to the runbook: "verify Dedicated burst capacity or schedule run during off-peak window" + automated rollback playbook link.

selena: I'll update the SOW template and share the legal-approved text in this thread. Customers who want expedited migration must sign the SOW before canary traffic begins.

priya: Decision: run two pilot migrations next sprint using the shim: one public model and one customer-specific pinned model (with SOW). Collect results for 30 days before standardizing. If both pilots meet thresholds we add shim as a migration path in the catalog lifecycle doc.

marc: I'll draft the BRI calculation and alert thresholds.

eric: I'll own runtime hooks for auto-fallback and capacity requests.

selena: I'll post SOW + pin-gracepath opt-in and the extended-pin pricing.

priya: Thanks all. I'll assemble the spec + runbook and post a link here. Meeting Tuesday 9am if we need a sync. :rocket:
